title: The practice's skills say what for in their descriptions and speak the pattern's terms in their bodies
situation: practice-restated: the seven skills of the cratylic-context-design practice (conceptualize, elicit, exemplify, formalize, materialize, probe, signify) were written before cratylic context design was stated; their descriptions say how, in notation, and their bodies cite the residue, the cold-decode oracle and signs, which the design names the semantic gap and its correction, the cold read and the term.
decision: Each skill's description states in plain words what the skill is for and when an agent reaches for it, in the pattern's terms (term, Cratylic name, semantic gap, missing and spurious meaning, correction, cold read), with no notation, no symbols and nothing of how cratylus builds or renders it. Each body keeps its formal statement and its procedure; only its terms are aligned: residue becomes the semantic gap where a name is judged and the correction where a concept enters a text beside its term, citing cratylic context design instead of workflow; a citation of the cold-decode oracle becomes the cold read; sign and signifier, where they mean a name, become term. The prime principle the skills open with restates cratylism as the design holds it: names natural to the model rather than conventional, each concept's Cratylic name the term leaving the smallest semantic gap in its context, found by a cold read, never coined where an established term covers it, its correction beside it; it cites no residue. Corpus and the canon's other unit words stay for their own later task, and the agents' stances, the cold-decode oracle among them, are untouched.
consequences: A session reading the skill list learns what each skill is for in the pattern's terms. One builder; review Ask.
